The Create retainer screen is built at `/#/new`. Lint, typecheck and the production build pass. I couldn't run an end-to-end wallet transaction here, because the sandbox has no wallet.

```
$ bash scripts/check.sh
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.   (oxlint, type-aware: src + scripts)
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.   (oxlint: whole project)
$ tsc --noEmit                   (clean)

$ bun run build
check-errors: all 26 ABI errors have a message.
$ tsc --noEmit
vite v6.4.5 building for production...
✓ 6425 modules transformed.
dist/assets/index-BgRcUHLB.js   1,465.19 kB │ gzip: 454.55 kB
✓ built in 14.30s
```
The build prints only the same third-party chunk-size notice as before.

**What the screen does**
- **Fields:** freelancer address, starting amount with your USDC balance beneath it, objection window, withdrawal notice, and end date.
- **Presets:** 5 minutes (demo), 24 hours, 48 hours and 7 days, plus Custom in hours. Window defaults to 48 hours and notice to 72 hours.
- **Notice presets:** I added a 72-hour option to the notice presets, because the spec's 72-hour default isn't one of the listed presets.
- **Validation:**
  - Checks run in the contract's order: freelancer, window, notice, end time.
  - The four limits are read from the deployed retainer, so the form can't disagree with it.
  - The end time must be strictly after chain time plus notice. Chain time comes from the chain-time hook, never your clock.
  - Amounts are parsed as exact 6-decimal integers.
  - A zero amount is allowed, as the contract allows it. An amount above your balance is blocked.
- **Summary sentence:** it restates the amount, end date, window and notice in plain terms. It says "If you stay silent, it pays out on its own", and says plainly when the window is an hour or less that a claim can pay out before you see it (ADR-010).
- **Actions:** these use the existing transaction hooks. **Approve X USDC** appears only when the allowance is below the exact amount, then **Create retainer**. Each button shows its own state: Checking…, Confirm in your wallet, then Creating retainer…. A revert is decoded before the wallet opens, failures show inline under the buttons, and Enter in a field runs the next step.
- **Navigation:** on success it reads the new retainer's number from the receipt and opens its page.
- **Toasts:** I used none, since navigating to the retainer is the confirmation.

**Checks against the live deployment:** I simulated `createRetainer` with the same argument types the screen sends. A 60-second window (the minimum) and a 30-day window with a 60-day notice both simulated fine. A 59-second window, a notice one second over 60 days, a freelancer equal to the caller and a zero freelancer each decoded to the right message. A 10 USDC deposit without approval decoded to "You don't have enough USDC approved or available."

**break-ui pass:** I ran the logic against your list. Layout at 320px is reasoned from the CSS only, because the sandbox has no browser; nothing was checked by eye.

| What broke | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| 0.000001 USDC read "0.00 USDC" in the summary and on the **Approve** button | New `formatUsdcPlain`: two decimals, or the exact value when there are more. |
| 1,000,000,000 USDC had no separators (`1000000000.00`) | Thousands separators on the whole part, in the shared amount formatter, so every screen gets them. |
| The date field could be wider than its container on narrow iOS screens | `.field` now has `min-width: 0` and `max-width: 100%`. |
| A half-typed address flashed red while typing | The error shows after you leave the field, or once 42 characters are in. |
| A 42-character address doesn't fit in 288px | The input scrolls, and the full checksummed address is also shown below it. |

These held up:
- **Pasted addresses:** whitespace, newlines, no-break spaces and zero-width characters around a pasted address are stripped. All-lowercase and all-uppercase hex are accepted. Mixed case must match its checksum, otherwise you get a typo message. A missing `0x`, `0X`, a name like `mara.eth` and 41 or 43 characters each get their own message.
- **Amounts:** `0.000001` parses to 1 base unit, and `1,000,000,000` parses exactly. Seven decimals are rejected. `1,000` is accepted but `1,5` and `1,00` are rejected as ambiguous.
- **Dates and limits:** an end date in the past, impossible dates and today with a 72-hour notice are rejected. The end time must be strictly after chain time plus notice. 720 hours (30 days) is accepted and 720.01 is not.

**One gap you should decide on:** a custom value is hours with at most two decimals, so the smallest custom window is 72 seconds. Exactly 60 seconds, the contract minimum, can't be typed. The 5-minute demo preset covers the demo. I can add a unit selector if you want it reachable.

There is no demo-data toggle in the build. I deleted both temporary test scripts. I did not touch `contracts/`, `deployments/`, `tracing.ts`, `console-capture.ts`, `README.md` or `AGENTS.md`, and I wrote no mainnet config.
